headline: Sensex Tumbles 600 Points as Global Chip Stock Retreat and Rising Crude Oil Prices Weigh on Sentiment

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Retreat in global chip stocks due to AI spending concerns in South Korean and Japanese markets
Crude oil prices rising above $110 per barrel impacting market pressure
Weak global cues with significant falls in the Nikkei and Kospi indices
Selling pressure in major heavyweights including Maruti Suzuki and Tata Steel
whatHappening: Sensex dropped over 600 points while Nifty tested the 22,600 support level
Jio Platforms IPO entered its second day of subscription with focus on GMP and lot size
IHCL reported a 22% year-on-year rise in Q2 revenue and increased its FY27 guidance
IT stocks are showing signs of a comeback supported by significant FII buying of Rs 6,500 crore
summary: The Indian stock market faced a sharp decline today, with the Sensex falling over 600 points amid global weakness and crude oil prices surpassing $110. Despite the broader sell-off, specific stocks like IHCL and Eternal gained on strong quarterly results and positive brokerage outlooks. Investors remain focused on the Jio Platforms IPO and a potential recovery in the IT sector driven by FII activity.
